name: student_wellness_s26
info: Ohlone College Student Well-Being Study, Spring 2026.
Survey responses collected April 27-May 1, 2026, during the 13th week of a 16-week semester.
This version keeps categorical variables with abbreviated ISLE-friendly response levels and keeps only one numerical variable: wellbeing_index.
The wellbeing_index is the average of the first 8 well-being survey items.

variables.student_id: Anonymous row ID for each survey response.
variables.life_direction_meaning: Q1: My life feels like it is moving in a direction that means something to me.
variables.college_work_resilience: Q2: When college work is difficult, I feel capable of finding a way through it.
variables.campus_seen_supported: Q3: At this college, I feel seen, respected, and supported.
variables.emotionally_steady: Q4: In my daily life, I generally feel emotionally steady and okay.
variables.hopeful_future: Q5: I feel hopeful about my future.
variables.clear_values: Q6: I have a clear sense of what really matters to me.
variables.life_depth_moments: Q7: I have moments that lift me out of routine and remind me that life is deeper than just getting through the day.
variables.cheerful_spirits: Q8: I feel cheerful and in good spirits much of the time.
variables.college_growth: Q9: My current college experience is contributing to meaningful growth, intellectually and personally.
variables.academic_wellbeing: Q10: Right now, school feels like it is going reasonably well for me academically.
variables.biggest_challenge: Q11: Biggest challenge making it harder to do one’s best as a student.
variables.school_time_energy: Q12: I have enough time and energy to do what school asks of me.
variables.faculty_staff_support: Q13: There is at least one faculty or staff member here who supports my growth.
variables.people_to_turn_to: Q14: When life gets hard, I have people I can turn to.
variables.know_support_resources: Q15: I understand how to find support at this college and feel able to make use of it when needed.
variables.focus_place: Q16: When I need to get schoolwork done, I usually have a place I can go and focus.
variables.enough_sleep: Q17: I usually get enough sleep to feel well rested.
variables.parent_caregiver_support: Q18: My relationship with my parent(s) or caregiver(s) is a source of support in my life.
variables.enjoyable_company: Q19: I get to be around people whose company I genuinely enjoy.
variables.feels_alone: Q20: Even when I am around people, I still feel alone.
variables.phone_social_media_interference: Q21: Phone or social media use interferes with my sleep or focus.
variables.physical_activity: Q22: I engage in physical activity or exercise.
variables.alcohol_cannabis_social_coping: Q23: Alcohol or cannabis are part of how I socialize, connect with others, or cope with stress.
variables.money_stress: Q24: How heavy money stress feels right now.
variables.study_hours_outside_class: About how many hours per week the student usually spends on schoolwork outside of class.
variables.life_priority: Q26: What feels most important in life right now.
variables.age_group: Student age group, using word labels such as 18 or 19 to avoid ISLE treating ranges as numbers.
variables.parent_four_year_college: Q31: Whether either parent/guardian graduated from a four-year college.
variables.college_goal: Q32: Main goal in college right now.
variables.major_field: Q33: College major or field of study.
variables.major_confidence: Q34: Confidence that current major or area of study is what the student wants to pursue.
variables.spring_credits: Number of college credits the student enrolled in during Spring Semester.
variables.class_modality: Q36: How most classes are being taken this Spring Semester.
variables.paid_work_hours: About how many hours per week the student works for pay.
variables.wellbeing_index: Average score from Q1-Q8 well-being items.
